key_insight: PIF-MIONet combines early fusion of multiple input functions with physics-informed learning to predict fluid flow within an FEM-coupled poroelasticity framework.
engineering_relevance: Coupling neural flow predictions with GEOS-based mechanical FEM offers a path toward more efficient large-scale poroelastic simulations.
method: Use IFENN to stagger mechanical-equilibrium FEM solves and neural fluid-flow predictions.
Fuse MIONet branch outputs to enable early interaction among input functions.
Combine physics and data losses, with domain decomposition for complex geometries and localized flow.
evidence_signal: Tests cover 2D and 3D domains, variable material properties and time discretizations, and unseen loading histories; for complex cases, physics-plus-data training used only 0.1% of the training increments used for purely data-driven training.
watch_item: Industrial-scale runtime gains and robustness of the staggered coupling are not quantified in the abstract.
paper_title: Physics-Informed Fusion-MIONet with IFENN: A Generalized Framework for Coupled Poroelasticity Problems
